name: University of Trento
summary: Public university in Trento, in the Alps; one law degree taught in English plus English tracks in computer science and engineering.

ib.text: A school diploma valid for university entry; a school letter saying your studies were taught in English proves the B2 English. Every English degree has capped places and an admission test.

programmes.name: Comparative, European and International Legal Studies (CEILS)
programmes.about: Law taught entirely in English with a comparative, European and international approach, plus a second European language; international students must take Italian.
programmes.overview: The degree rests on four foundations: comparative legal systems, European law, the historical and philosophical bases of modern legal thought, and substantive and procedural law in both private and public areas, always viewed through comparative, European and international lenses. Its distinctive feature is a comparative, international and transnational approach to law, preparing you to work across legal contexts. Alongside law you improve your English and study a second European language, German, French, Spanish or Italian. You can apply for internships in international institutions. Graduates are prepared for roles needing knowledge of several legal systems, especially in international organisations and EU settings.
programmes.ib: UniTrento's own admission test (online in session 1, in person in Trento in session 2); minimum 11/60. English B2.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on the admission test; a high score also cuts first-year fees (90/100+ pays none). EU places: 50 in session 1, 25 in session 2. 2026 criteria.

lastYear.text: apply to 6 March, test 23 March; or to 4 May, test 14 May

programmes.name: Computer Science (English track)
programmes.about: How to process, store and transmit information: maths, programming, algorithms, systems and data in the first two years, then subjects of your choice; runs in Italian or English.
programmes.overview: The first two years give you the basics: mathematics, programming and algorithms, and systems and information management, with software design and development. From the second year you add electives matched to your interests. Computer science is treated as a discipline between science and engineering, using scientific inquiry and rigorous engineering methods, and the degree is recognised by the Italian computer science professors' association and the national computing association. Typical early courses include calculus, discrete mathematics, programming, computer architecture, databases and operating systems. Graduates are prepared to design and develop software as an industry activity.
programmes.ib: CEnT-S (in English), taken by 31 March in session 1, minimum 16/45; later sessions use TOLC-I (in Italian).
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on your CEnT-S or TOLC-I score. EU CEnT-S places are only in session 1. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

lastYear.text: session 1: apply to 23 March; CEnT-S by 31 March

programmes.name: Computer, Communications and Electronic Engineering (English track)
programmes.about: Computer engineering, communications and electronics on a base of maths, physics and programming, strongly project- and lab-based; runs in Italian or English.
programmes.overview: The first year builds foundations in mathematical analysis, physics, programming, geometry and linear algebra, and after that you take transversal courses in three areas of specialisation: computer engineering, communications and electronics. Work is project-based, in laboratories using design equipment and software. Typical later courses include digital systems, signals, networks, electronic circuits and software engineering. Graduates usually work in information and communication technology and electronics companies or continue to a master's degree in engineering.
programmes.ib: CEnT-S (in English), taken by 31 March in session 1, minimum 16/45; later sessions use TOLC-I (in Italian).
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on your CEnT-S or TOLC-I score. EU CEnT-S places are only in session 1. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

lastYear.text: session 1: apply to 23 March; CEnT-S by 31 March

notes: The 2027-28 calls are not out yet; in 2026 applications opened in mid-December and the first session closed in March.
For the two English engineering and computing tracks, the English-language CEnT-S counts only in the first session; later sessions use the Italian TOLC-I.
As an EU applicant you can use every session; non-EU applicants abroad may apply only in the first one.
